label: Character pinning this one
summary: Each character whose player has pinned the scoped character.
details: Vanilla uses it once, with a death-management check, to add the matching characters to a list.

label: Previously played character
summary: Each character the player of this character has played before.
details: The character currently being played is left out. The game's documentation says the list matches the game's legacy feature, apart from that exclusion. Vanilla script does not use it.

label: Player
summary: Each player character in the game.
details: AI characters are skipped. It needs no starting scope and works anywhere. Vanilla uses it a lot to send events, toasts or messages to all human players.

label: Player heir
summary: Each heir of a player, counting only the first 10.
details: The game's documentation does not say whose heirs are meant. Vanilla uses it in court events on a character, checking for example whether an heir is the spouse of someone.

label: Legend in the library
summary: Each legend in the library of the player character.
details: The items are legends, not characters. Vanilla script does not use it.

label: Pledged attacker
summary: Each character who has pledged to the attacking side of a great holy war.
details: Runs on the great holy war. Vanilla uses it to check and reset the beneficiary of each attacker, to pick who may join the Frankokratia crusade, and to send an event.

label: Pledged defender
summary: Each character who has pledged to the defending side of a great holy war.
details: Runs on the great holy war. Vanilla uses it to add truces both ways with the title recipient, to collect human (non-AI) defenders in a list and to send them an event.

label: Pool character
summary: Each character in the character pool of a given province.
details: Vanilla uses it to pick local characters, for example peasants or candidates for a role, in a given province. You always write the province; vanilla gives it in every use. It needs no starting scope.

fields.name: province
fields.text: The province whose pool is searched.
fields.values: a province, for example the character's location or capital province

label: Pool guest
summary: Each guest at the character's court who came from the pool.
details: These guests have no liege, unlike foreign court guests. Vanilla uses it to pick guests for court events and to send them back to the pool.

label: Potential contributor
summary: Each character who could contribute to a great project contribution.
details: Who counts depends on the allowed contributor filter of the great project. The list is empty if the founder is dead or not a ruler, or if the contribution does not accept funding. Vanilla script does not use it.

label: Potential marriage option
summary: Each character offered as a selectable marriage or betrothal option.
details: The game's documentation does not say for whom the options are offered. Vanilla script does not use it.

label: Powerful family
summary: Each powerful family (house) in the character's realm.
details: The list is empty if the character is not independent. Vanilla uses it to find another house and its head, and to count powerful families.

label: Powerful vassal
summary: Each powerful vassal of the character.
details: Vanilla uses it to give opinion to major vassals, to notify them, and to order them by military strength or opinion.

label: Pretender title
summary: Each landed title the character is a pretender to.
details: Vanilla uses it once, checking the holder and the character's place in the line of succession.

label: Primary war enemy
summary: Each primary enemy in the character's wars.
details: The game's documentation does not define what makes an enemy primary. Vanilla uses it to pick an enemy to save for later, for example one who is at war as an attacker or one who is AI-controlled, and to check religion or top liege.

label: Prisoner
summary: Each character the scoped character holds in prison.
details: Vanilla uses it to release prisoners, to move them back to their default location, to trigger events for them and to pick one to save as a rival or other target.

label: Province
summary: Each land province in the game.
details: Sea and impassable provinces are skipped. It needs no starting scope. Vanilla uses it to loop over all holdings, to pick a random location and to check coastal provinces.

label: Province domicile
summary: Each domicile located in the scoped province.
details: Vanilla reads the owner of each domicile and tests whether it is an estate, what type it is and what buildings it has.

label: Province epidemic
summary: Each epidemic that affects the scoped province.
details: You can filter by how severe the outbreak is. Vanilla uses it mostly in triggers, for example to check the epidemic's trait or intensity.

fields.name: intensity
fields.text: Only epidemics with this outbreak intensity.
fields.values: an intensity such as apocalyptic, or a comparison like >= major

label: Province legend
summary: Each legend that affects the scoped province.
details: Vanilla uses it to find legends whose owner is somebody else, and to test a given legend.

label: Prowess councillor
summary: Each councillor whose position is based on prowess.
details: The game's documentation says only this, and vanilla script does not use it, so which positions count is not known.

label: Raid target
summary: Each ruler the character is hostile to because the character raided them.
details: Only the top lieges are returned, not their vassals. Vanilla uses it once, with only `always = yes`.

label: Real grandparent
summary: Each real grandparent of the character.
details: Going by the name, real probably means the actual grandparents rather than ones shown otherwise; the game's documentation only says real. Vanilla script does not use it.

label: Real great-grandparent
summary: Each real great-grandparent of the character.
details: Going by the name, real probably means the actual great-grandparents; the game's documentation only says real. Vanilla script does not use it.

label: Real parent
summary: Each of the two real parents of the character.
details: Going by the name, real probably means the actual parents; the game's documentation only says real. Vanilla script does not use it.

label: Realm border county
summary: Each county on the edge of the character's realm that borders another realm.
details: Vanilla uses it to add county modifiers, to order counties, and to pick one at random whose culture differs from a host's.

label: Realm county
summary: Each county in the character's realm.
details: The game's documentation says it is based on the top liege, so the realm is probably the whole realm under the top liege, vassals' counties included. Vanilla uses it a lot, for example to change county control, add modifiers and list counties.

label: Realm de jure duchy
summary: Each de jure duchy that has at least one county in the character's realm.
details: De jure means by the map's own borders, not by who holds it. The game's documentation says the realm is based on the top liege.

label: Realm de jure empire
summary: Each de jure empire that has at least one county in the character's realm.
details: De jure means by the map's own borders, not by who holds it. The game's documentation says the realm is based on the top liege.

label: Realm de jure kingdom
summary: Each de jure kingdom that has at least one county in the character's realm.
details: De jure means by the map's own borders, not by who holds it. The game's documentation says the realm is based on the top liege. Vanilla uses it to pick a target kingdom for a great holy war.

label: Realm province
summary: Each province in the character's realm.
details: Vanilla uses it to refill levies and garrisons, to start holdings and to check for free building slots.

label: Relation
summary: Each character the scoped character has a given scripted relation with.
details: Vanilla uses types such as friend, lover, rival, best friend, soulmate, guardian and blood brother. Someone who has several of the chosen relations appears only once. The game's documentation says you can name several types.

fields.name: type
fields.text: The relation type, or several types.
fields.values: a relation type such as friend, lover, rival, guardian

label: Related house
summary: Each of the two houses in a house relation.
details: Runs on a house relation and gives both houses. Vanilla often skips the character's own house to find the other one and then uses its head.

label: Religion
summary: Each religion in the game.
details: It needs no starting scope. Vanilla goes on from each religion into its faiths.

label: Head of faith challenger
summary: Each title that challenges the head of a faith.
details: Runs on a faith. Vanilla checks the holder and the sponsor of the challenger.

label: Required heir government
summary: Each government type that the heir must have for a holding type.
details: Vanilla uses it once, comparing with the government of a county holder.

label: County of the rite
summary: Each county of the rite.
details: Vanilla script does not use it.

label: Culture of the rite
summary: Each culture linked to the rite.
details: Vanilla script does not use it.

label: Duchy of the rite
summary: Each duchy with at least one county of the rite.
details: Vanilla script does not use it.

label: Empire of the rite
summary: Each empire with at least one county of the rite.
details: Vanilla script does not use it.

label: Hegemony of the rite
summary: Each hegemony with at least one county of the rite.
details: Vanilla script does not use it.

label: Kingdom of the rite
summary: Each kingdom with at least one county of the rite.
details: Vanilla script does not use it.

label: Tenet of the rite
summary: Each tenet of a rite, optionally only those with a given status in its faith.
details: The game's documentation names the core tenets of the rite. The status filter relates them to the rite's parent faith. Vanilla uses it to compare tenets before and after a faith changes.

fields.name: status
fields.text: Only tenets with this status for the parent faith.

label: Rite type
summary: Each rite type defined in the game.
details: It needs no starting scope. Vanilla script does not use it.

label: Ruler
summary: Each ruler of at least county rank in the game, optionally filtered.
details: Vassals are included unless you ask for independent rulers only. It needs no starting scope. The documented example names the filters government_type, tier and only_independent, but its list names government_type_filter and tier_filter, and vanilla uses faith_filter. Vanilla uses it to find rulers by culture or title tier and to send events.

fields.name: government_type_filter
fields.values: a government type, or a saved scope

fields.name: faith_filter
fields.values: a faith, or a saved scope

fields.name: culture_filter
fields.values: a culture, or a saved scope

fields.name: tier_filter
fields.text: Only rulers whose title has this tier.
fields.values: county, duchy, kingdom, empire or hegemony (baronies are not supported)

fields.name: only_independent
fields.text: Whether only independent rulers are listed.

label: Ruler in clerical region
summary: Each ruler whose realm capital lies in the clerical region.
details: Runs on a title. Vanilla uses it to find rulers to evangelize, skipping vassals of the root character.

label: Saint
summary: Each saint of a faith.
details: Vanilla uses it to read where a saint is buried, with a relic-extraction check.

label: Same-sex spouse candidate
summary: Each possible spouse of the same sex as the character.
details: The game warns that this is very slow, so do not use it often. Vanilla script does not use it.

label: Faith the artifact is sanctified for
summary: Each faith the scoped artifact is sanctified for.
details: The items are faiths, not characters. Vanilla script does not use it.

label: Scheme
summary: Each scheme the character owns, optionally only of one type.
details: Vanilla uses it to end schemes, to read their target, and to check their category.

fields.name: type
fields.values: a scheme type such as murder, seduce or befriend
